# Delivery probes — frozen, human-written

These files are the human half of the delivery oracle (board a6b118e4, layer 1).
`deriveExpected()` derives path-scoped expectations mechanically from the store;
it cannot derive a **subject-scoped** one, because H20's mechanism axis matches a
prompt's subject against rulings whose `file_keys` may name no file the prompt
mentions — which is the entire point of that surface. So the subject-scoped
expectations are written by hand, here.

## Two rules, both load-bearing

1. **Human-written, never generated from titles.** A probe generated by pasting a
   record's title back into a prompt measures string equality, not retrieval: it
   passes for a matcher that does nothing but substring-match, and it cannot fail
   in the way the mechanism actually fails. Every probe here uses the working
   vocabulary someone would really dispatch with, and the `note` field records
   what the author believed and why.
2. **Frozen.** A probe is not edited to make a run go green. If a probe's
   expectation is wrong, that is a finding to adjudicate — and the fix is to
   REPLACE the probe deliberately, with the reason in its `note`, or to fix the
   store. Repointing `expected_ids` at whatever was delivered turns the oracle
   into a mirror.

## Format

```
{
  "id":                  string, unique, matches the filename stem
  "kind":                "agent" | "ask" | "consult"
  "note":                string — why this probe exists and what it claims (human)
  "tool_input":          the VERBATIM shape of the real surface:
                           agent   -> { prompt, subagent_type, description }
                           ask     -> { questions: [{ question, header,
                                        options: [{ label, description }] }] }
                                      NO `prompt` field — AskUserQuestion has none
                                      (decision foreign_f5638a84); a synthesized one is a
                                      lie about the surface and is REFUSED by
                                      loadProbes()
                           consult -> { prompt }
  "expected_ids":        string[] — FULL uuids of records that must be delivered.
                         Required, even when empty: a probe with no expectation
                         can never fail.
  "expected_absent_ids": string[] — uuids that must NOT be delivered. This is what
                         makes a negative probe falsifiable.
  "expect_deny":         boolean — H20 must DENY this attempt (exit 2)
  "expect_deny_ids":     string[] — required when expect_deny is true; the ids the
                         denial must name. A deny expectation with no ids is
                         unfalsifiable and is REFUSED.
  "seed_ledger":         boolean, optional — do NOT wipe
                         .sterling/transient/delivery/ before this case. Only for
                         override/retry probes that need a prior denial to exist.
                         Default (absent) wipes the directory entirely, because a
                         stale deny ledger silently converts a first-attempt deny
                         into an allow.
}
```

## The arms, and why each one is here

- **probe-004-agent-positive-h15-cluster (positive)** — governed subject, delivery
  expected. Answers "does it fire when it should". Replaces the original
  probe-001-agent-positive (2026-09-08, decision
  h20-specificity-rebuild-not-fourth-patch-structural-fixes-now-red-probes-frozen):
  the H15 realpath/provenance cluster it targets grew after the probe was
  written, so its `expected_ids` were stale — see the probe's own `note` for
  which ids were added and why, and why b60b5cc5 is asserted ABSENT rather
  than simply omitted (it is the pin for the REVIEW-TERRITORY-line-stripping
  fix, not a genuine subject match).
- **probe-002 (deny)** — a first-attempt question whose subject the deny-once
  ruling itself settles. Answers "does the one blocking surface still block", and
  exercises the no-prompt `questions[]`/options shape.
- **probe-003 (near-miss negative)** — shared vocabulary, ungoverned subject.
  This is the CONTROL for the whole set: without it, a green positive is equally
  well explained by a matcher that fires on everything, and silence-by-default is
  H20's designed behaviour (AC10).

Add probes in pairs — a positive and the negative that could be confused with it.
A set of positives alone measures nothing about precision.
